html:
In April 1992 the communist government of Mohammad Najibullah collapsed and mujahideen forces entered Kabul.

Najibullah had outlasted the Soviet withdrawal of 1989, helped by Soviet arms and food. When the Soviet Union broke up and aid stopped at the start of 1992, his army began to dissolve. In March the Uzbek militia leader Abdul Rashid Dostum and others turned against him. Najibullah tried to fly out on 16 April, was stopped at the airport, and took refuge in the UN compound in Kabul.

Ahmad Shah Massoud's Panjshir forces and Dostum's men took the city between 25 and 28 April. Hekmatyar's fighters had also moved on Kabul from the south. Massoud's troops pushed them back, and the two sides were at war within days.

Najibullah stayed in the UN compound for four years. When the Taliban took Kabul in 1996 they dragged him out and killed him. The fall opened the civil war among the victors.
sum: In April 1992 the communist government of Mohammad Najibullah collapsed and mujahideen forces entered Kabul.
